lines.L02: On paper, a hundred-cell differential is easy to lose.
lines.L03: Under the oil objective, a stained blood film: red cells, platelets — and white cells.
lines.L04: Count where red cells touch but don’t overlap.
lines.L05: Segmented neutrophil: two to five lobes joined by thin strands, pale pink cytoplasm.
lines.L06: Band neutrophil: one curved nucleus, not divided into lobes.
lines.L07: Eosinophil: usually two lobes, packed with large orange-red granules.
lines.L08: Basophil: large, deep purple granules that cover the nucleus.
lines.L09: Lymphocyte: a round, dense nucleus with a thin blue rim.
lines.L10: Monocyte: the largest — a folded, kidney-shaped nucleus in grey-blue cytoplasm.
lines.L11: Move field by field in one direction, never back, so no cell is counted twice.
lines.L12: Classify each white cell as you meet it, until you reach {target}.
lines.L13: In LabGuide, every cell class has its own big button.
lines.L14: One tap adds one to that cell; a long press takes one away.
lines.L15: The total and every percentage update with each tap.
lines.L16: Choose 100 or 200 cells. At the target, counting stops…
lines.L17: …and an extra tap is not added.
lines.L18: Microscope mode: big screen zones, so your eyes stay on the eyepiece.
lines.L19: Each cell type has its own vibration pattern; every tenth cell, a longer signal.
lines.L20: Percent is count over total. With the WBC, absolute count is fraction times WBC.
lines.L21: Enter the WBC, and absolute counts appear next to each percentage.
lines.L22: Reference ranges come from your lab’s report form — and the comparison is not a diagnosis.
lines.L23: Save the result on this device, or copy it as text.
lines.L24: Keep your eyes on the cells. LabGuide keeps the count.

spoken.L16: Choose one hundred or two hundred cells. At the target, counting stops…
spoken.L20: Percent is count over total. With the W B C, absolute count is fraction times W B C.
